config.title: CSS Modules

intro.title: CSS Modules
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that uses CSS Modules to style its elements. You will learn how CSS Modules work by scoping styles locally to a component, preventing conflicts with other parts of your application. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and CSS Modules with file naming conventions like .component.css. This approach helps you write maintainable and modular CSS in your Angular projects.
intro.usecase: CSS Modules are essential in large-scale Angular applications where component styling must be isolated and predictable. You'll use them when building reusable UI libraries, dashboard widgets, or complex forms where each component's styles shouldn't interfere with others. For example, a financial dashboard with multiple independent chart components, or an e-commerce product filter panel where each filter needs distinct styling without global CSS conflicts. This pattern ensures your styles remain scoped to their components, making maintenance and team collaboration much easier in real production environments.

objectives: Apply CSS Modules to style Angular components with scoped selectors
Configure Angular to process CSS Modules for component-specific styling
Bind CSS class names from modules to component templates
Manipulate component styles using imported CSS Module objects
Integrate CSS Modules with existing Angular component architecture
Construct reusable styling patterns using CSS Modules methodology
Update component styling by modifying CSS Module files

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both symbols from the Angular core module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing Angular core symbols
import { Component, NgModule } from '@angular/core';
steps.expectedOutcome: The Angular core dependencies Component and CommonModule are imported, enabling component creation and module functionality.
successCriteria: Component and CommonModule are imported from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Please import both Component and CommonModule from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create a new Angular component with CSS module support
steps.instruction: Create an Angular component class named 'CssModulesDemo' with a template and styleUrls pointing to a CSS module file named 'css-modules-demo.component.css'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator with selector, template, and styleUrls properties. The styleUrls should reference the CSS module file.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Create your CssModulesDemo component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named CssModulesDemo is created with proper Angular component metadata including a template and CSS module reference.
successCriteria: Component class CssModulesDemo is defined with @Component decorator containing selector, template, and styleUrls pointing to 'css-modules-demo.component.css'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the component, but it's missing some required elements. Make sure to include the @Component decorator with selector, template, and styleUrls properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Remember to define a class named CssModulesDemo with the @Component decorator that includes selector, template, and styleUrls properties.

steps.title: Generate the CSS module file for the component
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file named 'css-modules-demo.component.module.css' in the same directory as your component file.
steps.hint: The file should have a .module.css extension to enable CSS Modules functionality in Angular.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Create your CssModulesDemo component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS module file is created with the correct naming convention for your component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You created a CSS file, but make sure it has the .module.css extension for Angular CSS Modules.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS module file wasn't created. Create a file named 'css-modules-demo.component.module.css' in your component directory.

steps.title: Add basic CSS classes to the module file
steps.instruction: Open the CSS module file (css-modules-demo.component.module.css) and define two CSS classes: one named 'title' with a large font size and bold weight, and another named 'content' with a smaller font size and a different text color.
steps.hint: In the .module.css file, write standard CSS rules. For example: .title { font-size: 24px; font-weight: bold; } .content { font-size: 16px; color: #333; }
steps.seedCode:
/* css-modules-demo.component.module.css */
/* Add your CSS classes here */
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS module file will contain two locally scoped CSS classes that can be applied to elements in your component.
successCriteria: The CSS module file contains at least two CSS class definitions (.title and .content) with appropriate styling properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some CSS, but make sure you have both .title and .content classes defined with appropriate styling properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS module file doesn't contain the required class definitions. Please add .title and .content classes with CSS properties.

steps.title: Import the CSS module into the component TypeScript file
steps.instruction: In the component TypeScript file, import the CSS module file and assign it to a variable named 'styles'.
steps.hint: Use a named import to bring in the CSS module object. The import path should be './css-modules-demo.component.module.css'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a CSS module in Angular
import styles from './my-component.module.css';
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS module is imported as a TypeScript object that can be used to reference CSS classes in the component.
successCriteria: The CSS module file is imported and assigned to a variable named 'styles'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing from the correct path and assigning it to a variable named 'styles'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS module import is missing or incorrect. Check the import path and variable assignment.

steps.title: Define a template variable for the CSS module object
steps.instruction: In the CssModulesDemoComponent class, create a public property named 'styles' to hold the imported CSS module object.
steps.hint: Add a public property in the component class that references the imported CSS module.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a public property that makes the CSS module classes available in the template.
successCriteria: A public property named 'styles' is defined in the component class and assigned the imported CSS module object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've created a public property named 'styles' that references the imported CSS module.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have a public property named 'styles' that exposes the CSS module object.

steps.title: Create the component template structure
steps.instruction: Create the component's template file (css-modules-demo.component.html) and add a div element as the root container.
steps.hint: Create a new HTML file in the same directory as your component. Start with a simple div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: A template file is created with a div element as the root container.
successCriteria: The css-modules-demo.component.html file exists and contains a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created the HTML file and added a div element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template file or div element is missing. Create css-modules-demo.component.html with a div element.

steps.title: Apply CSS module classes to template elements
steps.instruction: In the component's template (css-modules-demo.component.html), apply the 'container' CSS module class to the existing <div> element using Angular's class binding syntax.
steps.hint: Use property binding with [class] and reference the imported styles object (e.g., styles.container).

steps.title: Add multiple elements with different CSS module classes
steps.instruction: Add two new <div> elements inside the existing wrapper <div>, each with a different CSS module class applied from the imported styles object.
steps.hint: Use the styles object you imported earlier to access your CSS classes. Apply one class to the first new <div> and a different class to the second new <div>.

steps.title: Verify CSS module scoping in the browser
steps.instruction: Run the Angular application using `ng serve` and open it in your browser. Use the browser's developer tools to inspect the elements in your component and verify that the CSS module classes have been transformed into unique, scoped class names.
steps.hint: Look at the generated HTML in the Elements/Inspector tab. The class names on your elements should look something like '_header_abc123' instead of just 'header'.
